open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure boundary
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them.” conflicts with “An agent's own access to a service — as for processing a photo (decision 17) — is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel; ... its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on an agent receiving personal-data content apply only to kernel responses, or also to the agent's direct access to microservices?
options: Only kernel responses are restricted; direct service access may expose personal-data content to the agent
The prohibition is global, so direct service access must also return only digest and class
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as a kernel-surface promise only, because the changed exclusion says so explicitly.

open_points.subject: file access through the kernel
open_points.text: “never through the kernel, which hands no caller a file” conflicts with M22 and A10 rule 2, which say the owner may inspect a spooled file's bytes while the run holds them, and A16 rule 3, which also permits owner-only reading of trial-fixture bytes.
open_points.question: Is owner inspection allowed to return spooled-file and trial-fixture bytes, or does the new statement prohibit the kernel from returning file bytes to every caller?
options: Keep owner-only byte inspection and read “hands no caller a file” as referring only to flow inputs and outputs or to agents
Prohibit all file-byte responses, including the owner inspection described by M22, A10 and A16
open_points.default_guess: Keep the explicit owner-only inspection operations and interpret the new phrase narrowly as prohibiting agent access and file-valued flow I/O.

open_points.subject: credential echoes inside file responses
open_points.text: “one that carries it ... inside a file the kernel only moves, cannot be recognised” conflicts with A09 rule 7: “Every body as read, whatever its status ... is searched ... for the bytes of the credential value sent with the request,” and with A17 rule 2, which withholds a response body that echoes the credential verbatim.
open_points.question: Must the kernel scan file-response bodies for a verbatim credential before spooling them, or must files be moved without content inspection so such an echo is not recognised?
options: Scan every HTTP response body, including file outputs, and withhold a file containing the credential bytes
Do not scan file-output bodies; protect an embedded credential only through the file's disclosure class
open_points.default_guess: Follow the changed State 0 text and K-10's no-content-inspection rule: do not scan file outputs, while continuing to scan non-file response bodies.

open_points.subject: MCP listener and reverse-proxy exclusivity
open_points.text: “The proxy terminates TLS and is the only client of the kernel's listener, whose address the installation names and which the host does not expose otherwise” is not accompanied by a State 2 restriction or check on `mcp_listen_address`; A17 accepts the configured address and the kernel authenticates any client presenting a valid token.
open_points.question: What makes the reverse proxy the listener's only possible client: must the kernel restrict the listener to a Unix socket or loopback address, must it authenticate the proxy separately, or is non-exposure solely an unchecked host invariant?
options: Restrict accepted listener addresses to a locally protected Unix socket or loopback endpoint
Add a kernel-verifiable proxy authentication or peer check
Treat proxy-only reachability as an external host obligation that the kernel neither checks nor guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an external host obligation, since the text assigns exposure to the host and specifies no kernel-side proxy identity mechanism.
